subject: Demo alignment + throughput sizing — next steps
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Finex discovery — next step: demo & throughput sizing

Tom — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock the technical deep dive + dedicated capacity sizing: 

Summary (from our discovery)
- Primary use: customer support summarization + fraud-detection reranking on incoming messages
- Rough QPS estimate: 60–120 peak concurrent requests, spiking for batch reports
- Typical request length: 256–1024 tokens (many ~400)
- Latency target: p95 < 300ms for synchronous API calls

Proposed next step: 60–90 minute dedicated sizing + demo session where we:
1) Walk through a short Redwood demo focused on latency optimizations
2) Review Finex load profile and sample requests
3) Map to dedicated GPU pool sizing and autoscale guardrails

Please let us know preferred windows (we've blocked a few tentative slots):
- Mon Jul 17, 10:00–11:30 PDT
- Tue Jul 18, 14:00–15:30 PDT
- Wed Jul 19, 08:00–09:30 PDT

Prep items list (if you can share ahead of the call):
- Peak qps and average qps (CSV or short doc)
- A handful of representative payloads (anonymized)
- Latency SLOs and any hard SLAs

I'll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm a slot. Attendees from our side: me, Marissa (solutions), Ben (capacity lead).

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

—
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.com

Attachments: finex_capacity_template.xlsx (blank worksheet to capture qps/seq lengths)
From: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@finex.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Jul 2028 17:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Finex discovery — next step: demo & throughput sizing

Thanks, Dylan — great summary. We can do Tue Jul 18 at 14:00 PDT; that works for our engineering lead (Sara Kim) and me. 

We have a recent load-export (CSV) and a set of anonymized requests — I'll upload them to the Drive link you sent. Two quick questions before the call: 
1) Do you need raw logs or a tokenized sample? We can provide both but want to avoid extra work if tokenized is sufficient.
2) For the demo, are you planning to show caching/batching strategies or keep it focused on out-of-the-box latency?

If you confirm the agenda and what you need from us, we'll make sure Sara is prepped.

Tom
VP Product, Finex
Tom.Ellis@finex.com
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@finex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Finex discovery — next step: demo & throughput sizing

Perfect — locking Tue Jul 18, 14:00–15:30 PDT. I've created a provisional calendar event and shared a short prep folder: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/finex-demo-prep (I'll attach the template to this thread).

Answers to your questions: 
- Tokenized samples are great if available; raw logs are also useful for throughput curves. Either works — tokenized reduces prep on our side.
- We'll split the demo: first 25–30 minutes on a focused latency demo (including continuous batching behavior), then 30–40 minutes on sizing: throughput curves, KV/prefix caching impact, and recommended dedicated pool configuration. We'll explicitly call out tradeoffs for quantization and inference parallelism.

Prep checklist for Finex (if you can drop these into the Drive before Tue):
- Peak qps and average qps CSV
- 10–20 anonymized request examples (tokenized preferred)
- Any latency SLO doc or notes

Attachments: redwood-demo-guide.pdf, finex_capacity_template.xlsx
Calendar: https://calendar.redwood.com/event/1a2b3c4d

See you Tuesday — I'll invite Sara to the event.

—
Dylan
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tom Ellis <t.ellis@finex.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Finex discovery — next step: demo & throughput sizing

Thanks all — good plan. A couple internal notes for our prep: 
- I'll reserve a dedicated GPU pool for the Tue slot (N+1 capacity) so we can run a couple of guided experiments if Finex provides representative payloads.
- On the call, please highlight whether p95 or p99 is the primary SLO; that changes the starting pool size assumption.
- Quick ask to Finex: if you're planning to enable prefix caching, note the percent of repeat prefixes (even a rough estimate is helpful).

If Tom/Sara drop the CSV and examples into the Drive by EOD Mon, we'll be in a great spot.

Ben
Capacity Solutions, Redwood Inference
--- End of thread ---
